Least-squares measurement model

Source: R/leastsquares.R
leastsquares.Rd

A function of class "terradish_measurement_model" that evaluates a Gaussian likelihood with independent errors and a linear mean structure relating observed genetic distances to resistance distances. This is the fastest measurement model and a useful exploratory or diagnostic choice. For distance-response inference, mlpe represents shared-site dependence that this model omits.

Usage

leastsquares(
  E,
  S,
  phi,
  nu = NULL,
  gradient = TRUE,
  hessian = TRUE,
  partial = TRUE,
  nonnegative = TRUE,
  validate = FALSE
)

Arguments

E

Conductance-implied covariance matrix: the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian, evaluated at the current conductance parameters. Passed automatically by the optimizer; users normally do not call this function directly.

S

Square, symmetric matrix of observed pairwise genetic distances (e.g. \(F_{ST}\)). Must have the same dimensions as E.

phi

Named numeric vector of nuisance parameters (alpha, beta, tau). Omit to obtain maximum-likelihood starting values from an nlme::gls fit.

nu

Unused; present for a common interface with Wishart measurement models.

gradient

Logical. Compute gradient of the negative log-likelihood with respect to phi?

hessian

Logical. Compute Hessian of the negative log-likelihood with respect to phi?

partial

Logical. Compute second partial derivatives with respect to phi, E, and S? Required by the optimizer; set FALSE only for standalone likelihood evaluations.

nonnegative

Logical. Constrain the IBR slope beta to be nonnegative? Default TRUE prevents a nonsensical negative resistance-distance slope.

validate

Logical. Numerically validate gradients and Hessians via numDeriv? Very slow; intended for debugging small examples only.

Value

When phi is missing, a list with elements phi (starting values), lower, and upper (parameter bounds). Otherwise a list containing:

objective

Negative log-likelihood.

fitted

Matrix of expected genetic distances (same dimensions as S).

boundary

Logical; TRUE if the MLE is on the boundary (beta = 0), indicating no detectable IBR signal.

gradient

Gradient of the negative log-likelihood with respect to phi (if gradient = TRUE).

hessian

Hessian matrix with respect to phi (if hessian = TRUE).

gradient_E

Gradient with respect to E (if partial = TRUE).

partial_E

Jacobian of gradient_E with respect to phi (if partial = TRUE).

partial_S

Jacobian of gradient with respect to the lower triangle of S (if partial = TRUE).

jacobian_E

Function for reverse-mode algorithmic differentiation through E (if partial = TRUE).

jacobian_S

Function for reverse-mode algorithmic differentiation through S (if partial = TRUE).

Details

The nuisance parameters are:

alpha

Intercept of the regression of genetic distance on resistance distance.

beta

IBR slope; constrained \(\geq 0\) when nonnegative = TRUE.

tau

Log-precision of the Gaussian errors: residual variance is \(\exp(-\tau)\), so the residual standard deviation is exp(-tau / 2). In the Wishart measurement models tau denotes a different quantity (see wishart_covariance).

The mean structure is \(S_{ij} = \alpha + \beta R_{ij} + e_{ij}\), where \(R_{ij}\) is the resistance distance between sites \(i\) and \(j\) (derived from E) and \(e_{ij}\) are independent Gaussian errors with common precision \(\exp(\tau)\).

Pairwise genetic distances are not independent: any two pairs sharing a sampling site can be correlated. leastsquares ignores this dependence, so its standard errors can be too small. Use it for fast exploration, diagnostics, or initial parameter searches rather than as the default basis for distance-response inference.

See also

mlpe, generalized_wishart, wishart_covariance, terradish

Other measurement models: generalized_wishart(), mlpe(), mlpe_covariates(), pairwise_covariates(), pairwise_endpoint_covariates(), terradish_measurement_model, wishart_covariance(), wishart_covariates()

Examples

library(terra)

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

# Graph covariance (generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian) among the
# focal sites under uniform conductance (all coefficients zero).
laplacian_inv <- terradish_distance(theta = matrix(0, 1, 2),
                                    formula = ~ forestcover + altitude,
                                    data = surface,
                                    covariance = TRUE)$covariance[, , 1]

# Without 'phi': starting values and bounds for the nuisance parameters
leastsquares(laplacian_inv, Fst)
#> $phi
#>      alpha       beta        tau 
#> 0.01002299 0.22923592 6.47733469 
#> 
#> $lower
#> [1] -Inf    0 -Inf
#> 
#> $upper
#> [1] Inf Inf Inf
#> 
# With 'phi': the negative log-likelihood and derivatives at those values
value <- leastsquares(laplacian_inv, Fst,
                      phi = c(alpha = 0, beta = 0.5, tau = -0.1))
value$objective
#> [1] 25.83699
